scholarships.title: Killam Predoctoral Scholarship Level 2 (Doctoral)
scholarships.official_source: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Graduate Studies

existing.description: The Faculty of Graduate Studies at Dalhousie University awards Killam Predoctoral Scholarships competitively to outstanding doctoral students across all disciplines, with a base value of $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years. The scholarship is open to both Canadian and international students in a full-time PhD at Dalhousie, and international recipients may only use the funds for study and research in Canada. Applicants who are not eligible to apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D through Dalhousie in the current competition apply through the Faculty of Graduate Studies scholarship platform. The scholarship is supported by the Killam Trusts.
eligibility: Enrolled in a full-time doctoral (PhD) degree at Dalhousie University
Demonstrates exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in their field
Award taken up no later than the 7th term in the PhD program

Has spent less than six terms (24 months) in the PhD as of May 1 of the award year; for students who transferred or intend to transfer from a Master's to a PhD without completing the Master's, time-in-program begins at the transfer date
existing.eligibility_summary: Full-time doctoral (PhD) students at Dalhousie University, Canadian or international. Applicants must demonstrate exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in their field, with character, ethical conduct and contributions to a respectful and inclusive community also considered. The award must be taken up no later than the 7th term of the PhD, and applicants must have spent fewer than six terms (24 months) in the PhD as of May 1 of the award year.
benefits: Base value $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years
If a Tri-agency CGRS-D is awarded, the CGRS-D value of $40,000 per year is topped up to $48,000 per year ($16,000 per term) while both awards are held concurrently
If the CGRS-D expires before the end of the award holder's fourth year in the PhD, Killam funding is extended into the remaining terms of the fourth year at $14,000 per term
Relocation allowance reimbursing travel to Nova Scotia, not exceeding the lowest cost airfare available by the most direct route
Paid parental leave benefits for predoctoral Killam scholars without access to other paid parental leave support
Non-paid interruption of the award for up to 12 months for an approved leave of absence, with the end date extended by the leave duration
coverage: Cash stipend of $42,000 per year ($14,000 per term) for up to three years
Relocation travel reimbursement for new scholars relocating to Nova Scotia, capped at the lowest cost airfare by the most direct route
Paid parental leave benefits for predoctoral Killam scholars who lack other paid parental leave support
requirements: Submit the application and all accompanying materials by the stated round deadline, after which the application closes

Non-Tri-agency applicants create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform under Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and the category Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
Dalhousie students with a NetID access the platform using their Dalhousie NetID
Complete an annual report and submit it to fgs.slo@dal.ca by July 31 of each year the award is held
Apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D within the first two years of holding the Killam award
Participate in Killam scholar initiatives and events whenever possible
application_method: Applicants who submitted or intend to submit a Tri-agency CGRS-D application through Dalhousie in the current cycle are automatically considered for Killam funding

Applicants not eligible for a CGRS-D through Dalhousie create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform, selecting Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
existing.selection_notes: Awards are made competitively on the basis of exceptional academic achievement, strong research potential and a clear likelihood of contributing to the advancement of learning in the field; considerations beyond academic excellence include character, ethical conduct and contributions to a respectful and inclusive community.
existing.best_fit: Early-stage PhD students at Dalhousie with exceptional academic records and strong research potential who are not eligible for a CGRS-D through the university in the current cycle, or who wish to be considered for both.
existing.notes: The Killam scholarship becomes partially or fully honorary in terms where the recipient also holds other Faculty of Graduate Studies managed awards, including CGRS-D, Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarships and Abdul Majid Bader Graduate Scholarships. Additional supervisor or department stipends do not directly reduce Killam funding, although departments may adjust package arrangements at their discretion. Relocation reimbursements must be claimed by the end of the first term and do not cover family members or personal effects. Funding is provided by the Killam Trusts and administered by the Dalhousie Faculty of Graduate Studies.
existing.application_period: Round one is open now and closes October 16, 2026 at midnight Atlantic Time; round two opens January 5, 2027 and closes February 28, 2027 at midnight AT. These rounds are stated for non-Tri-agency applicants.
existing.deadline_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT

scholarships.title: Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship (DRES)
scholarships.official_source: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Graduate Studies

existing.description: Established in 2024, the Dalhousie Research Excellence Scholarship attracts and supports exceptional new PhD students at Dalhousie University and is valued at $35,000 per year for up to four years. Of the total, $28,000 is provided by Graduate Studies and the remaining $7,000 by the supervisor and/or programme of study. Applicants must intend to start a PhD at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028, and funds are only administered after admission to and registration in the intended programme. Applicants who apply for a Tri-agency CGRS-D through Dalhousie in the current cycle are considered automatically for DRES funding.
eligibility: Intent to start, meaning enrol in or transfer to, a PhD programme at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028
Capacity to generate significant regional, national or international impact through their research
Scholarship funds are only administered after admission to and registration in the intended programme of study
existing.eligibility_summary: New PhD students at Dalhousie intending to enrol in or transfer to a PhD programme between January 2027 and January 2028, from Canada or abroad. Applicants must demonstrate outstanding research achievement, exceptional leadership potential, and the capacity to generate significant regional, national or international impact through their research.
benefits: $35,000 per year for up to four years, maintained while the award holder stays eligible
Automatic top-up to $42,000 per year while a Killam Predoctoral Scholarship is held concurrently
Possibility of additional funding beyond the award value through stipends or other sources negotiated with the supervisor or programme of study
coverage: Cash funding of $35,000 per year for up to four years, of which $28,000 comes from Graduate Studies and $7,000 from the supervisor and/or programme of study
Hold period of up to 48 months, ending no later than the end of the fourth year in the programme
Top-up to the Killam value of $42,000 per year when held concurrently with a Killam Predoctoral Scholarship
requirements: Submit the application and all accompanying materials by the round deadline, after which the application form closes

Non-Tri-agency applicants create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform under Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and the category Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
Dalhousie students access the platform using their Dalhousie NetID
Complete an annual report and submit it to fgs.slo@dal.ca by July 31 of each year the award is held
Apply to the Tri-agency CGRS-D competition within the first two years of the PhD programme
Students planning to transfer from a master's to a PhD must apply for a doctoral scholarship before officially transferring into the doctoral programme
application_method: Applicants who submitted or intend to submit a Tri-agency CGRS-D application through Dalhousie in the current cycle are automatically considered for DRES funding

Applicants not eligible for a CGRS-D through Dalhousie create an application in the Faculty of Graduate Studies Scholarship Management Platform, selecting Major Scholarship Competitions 2026/2027 and Major Scholarship Application for Non-Tri-Agency Applicants
existing.selection_notes: The award targets applicants demonstrating outstanding research achievement, exceptional leadership potential, and the capacity to generate significant regional, national or international impact through their research. Recipients are expected to contribute innovative research with potential for significant impact.
existing.best_fit: Prospective doctoral students with a strong research record and leadership experience who intend to begin a PhD at Dalhousie between January 2027 and January 2028.
existing.notes: Time in programme for funding eligibility is based on the effective transfer date for students transferring from a master's to a PhD without completing the master's. Successful CGRS-D applicants receive the full CGRS-D value of $40,000 per year, and DRES becomes honorary while both awards are held concurrently. DRES recipients may also receive additional funding beyond the award value through stipends or other sources negotiated with their supervisor or programme of study.
existing.duration: Up to 48 months, and not past the end of the fourth year in the programme
existing.application_period: Round one of the non-Tri-agency competition is open until October 16, 2026 at midnight Atlantic Time; round two opens January 5, 2027 and closes February 28, 2027 at midnight AT. Intended PhD start must fall between January 2027 and January 2028.
existing.deadline_display: Round one: October 16, 2026 at midnight AT. Round two: opens January 5, 2027, submissions due February 28, 2027 at midnight AT
